quotes.text: 1812 West Muhammad Ali Boulevard is significant within the context of the Russell National District which was listed in 1980, This structure is typical of shotgun houses that were built throughout this particular neighborhood (as well as throughout Louisville) during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Houses with this floor plan were routinely built for the common man as worker housing. quotes.text: 1812 West Muhammad Ali Boulevard is a single-story Italianate style house built with a shotgun floor plan (see attached Sanborn Insurance Map). It is constructed of brick but form stone has been applied to the primary facade. It has a two bay facade arrangement with the door to the west balanced by a window to the east. Both have prominent segmentally arched hoods.

quotes.text: The building's cornice is elaborately detailed with sawn wood Gothic bargeboard pendles. A front facing gabled roof covered with asphalt shingles tops the building.

measurements.note: A door and one window: the whole public face of the household, and the eight feet of frontage the node's own prose describes.

note: The plain, surveyed, undated one. It is here because the corpus's shotgun node argues that the type absorbed whatever ornament the era offered and concentrated all of it on the street gable, and this survey says exactly that in a federal document: Italianate hoods, a sawn Gothic bargeboard cornice, and a two-bay front on a house whose plan is a file of rooms. The form stone on the facade is the same instinct a century later.
